Selection barriers

Why a broad 'recovery after illness' claim is inadequate

Stroke rehabilitation, postoperative recovery and paediatric services differ in their clinical pathways. A useful recommendation must distinguish regulated medical rehabilitation from general wellness and unsupported outcome claims.

01

The stage of care is missing

Early, inpatient and outpatient rehabilitation are not interchangeable. A fitness or wellness programme should not be described as specialist medical rehabilitation without supporting evidence.

02

Age and clinical profile are unclear

Separate adult and paediatric regulations apply. Eligibility, contraindications and clinical recommendations are determined by the provider, not a search summary.

03

Recovery claims lack a basis

Promises of a complete recovery within a fixed number of weeks need robust and relevant clinical evidence. Descriptions must not imply guaranteed patient outcomes.

Verifiable facts

Evidence I verify before making service claims

Article 40 of Russian Federal Law 323-FZ defines medical rehabilitation. Order 788n, updated in 2025, covers adults; Order 878n addresses children. For relevant medical services I also check the provider's licence record in the Roszdravnadzor register.

  • Actual clinical programme, licensed work, age range, care stage and location-specific admission
  • Team composition, equipment, referral process and documented clinical service scope
  • Published prices for defined services, programme content, dates and permission to publish case details

Regulations establish service requirements, not proof of treatment outcomes at a particular provider. No GAEO rehabilitation client success is claimed here.

Scope of work

How I run GEO for rehabilitation providers

I distinguish adult, paediatric and referring-professional questions, then compare AI answers with verifiable service evidence and consistent BMR measurement.

  1. 01

    Unbranded BMR baseline

    Record care-stage, clinical profile, age and location queries with current recommendations and cited sources.

  2. 02

    Check clinical evidence

    Verify the licence, scope, team, admission requirements and accuracy of programme claims without patient guarantees.

  3. 03

    Improve service information

    Prepare briefs for programmes, specialists, locations, admissions, prices and permitted educational materials.

  4. 04

    Measure again

    Repeat the prompt set and review BMR and accuracy by age, medical profile and stage of care.

FAQ

Questions about the service

Can adult and paediatric rehabilitation use identical landing pages?+

No. There are distinct organisational requirements and demand scenarios. Each programme needs accurate age eligibility and referral information.

Does every wellness centre qualify as medical rehabilitation?+

No. Check the actual service, documentation and the relevant legal status before presenting it as medical care.

How can a centre's licence be checked?+

Consult the official register for the specific organisation, address and authorised scope of medical activity.

Can rehabilitation providers promise a full recovery?+

No individual result can be guaranteed. Accurate content describes programmes, eligibility and limitations without promising clinical outcomes.

How much does GAEO charge rehabilitation centres?+

Published GAEO plans apply. Scope varies by programme, location, audience and the initial buyer-prompt matrix.
